rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's adornment consoles the Prophet over the idolators' rejection: God granted worldly beauty hoping for gratitude, but their ingratitude would bring its removal and barren lands, alluding to seven famine years like Joseph's.
rows.anchor: والذي يبدو : أنها تسلية للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم على إعراض المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence beginning with inna explains the consolation in verse 6 and connects to the warning of severe punishment in verse 2.
rows.anchor: وموقع ( إن ) في صدر هذه الجملة موقع التعليل للتسلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reversal between earthly life and death recalls God's power over opposites and teaches people not to trust strength, but to prepare for changing states and judge themselves by virtue and good outcomes.
rows.anchor: ويحصل من ذلك تذكير بعضهم قدرة الله تعالى ، وخاصة ما كان منها إيجادا للأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is the closest sign to human perception and reflection, as other verses likewise direct people to observe the earth and creation.
rows.anchor: وأوثر الاستدلال بحال الأرض التي عليها الناس لأنها أقرب إلى حسهم وتعقلهم ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording compresses several purposes: gratitude for a world fitted with beautiful adornments and recognition of God's artistry, as in other descriptions of worldly beauty.
rows.anchor: الامتنان على الناس والتذكير ببديع صنع الله إذ وضع هذا العالم على أتقن مثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause completes the lesson by confirming the world's eventual end; ja'ilun is an active participle used for the future, when all earthly life becomes dry, bare soil.
rows.anchor: تكميل للعبرة وتحقيق لفناء العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sa'id means soil, while juruz means barren and bare; the meaning of sa'id is revisited at verse 40.
rows.anchor: والصعيد : التراب . والجرز : القاحل الأجرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am marks a transition from the introduction to the surah's central subject; it is not an abrupt shift because the cave story answers the Prophet's grief over rejection.
rows.anchor: للإضراب الانتقالي من غرض إلى غرض . ولما كان هذا من المقاصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story answers deniers who rejected resurrection: the sleepers' awakening after a long interval exemplifies its possibility.
rows.anchor: فكان ذكر أهل الكهف وبعثهم بعد خمودهم سنين طويلة مثالا لإمكان البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am is disconnected, meaning bal, and requires an understood interrogative; here the implied question expresses amazement, with a line by Afnun al-Taghlibi illustrating the construction.
rows.anchor: المنقطعة بمعنى ( بل ) ، وهي ملازمة لتقدير الاستفهام معها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied question asks whether the sleepers are more astonishing than God's other signs; reviving the dead is more wondrous because it restores no retained life, unlike sleep.
rows.anchor: فإن إماتة الأحياء بعد حياتهم أعظم من عجب إنامة أهل الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage rebukes people who ask about a marvel while rejecting the still greater marvel of the world's end; they deny any life beyond this world and blame time for death.
rows.anchor: بأنهم سألوا عن عجيب وكفروا بما هو أعجب ، وهو انقراض العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listeners should move from curiosity about extraordinary stories to their lessons: the youths' prayer and steadfast faith expose idolatry and model the conduct their questioners should follow.
rows.anchor: وفيه لفت لعقول السائلين عن الاشتغال بعجائب القصص إلى أن الأولى لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the Prophet but intends his Meccan questioners and the People of the Book who prompted them; Ibn Ashur thinks the question may have been suggested by Christians connected to Mecca.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للنبيء . والمراد : قومه الذين سألوا عن القصة ، وأهل الكتاب الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among Our signs means the sleepers are one of many wonders, not uniquely astonishing; alternatively, the phrase can mean astonishing within the signs, exposing the questioners' poor judgment.
rows.anchor: فمعنى ( من ) في قوله : { من آياتنا } التبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the sleepers themselves astonishing omits the word state, and using the abstract noun intensifies the description of their astonishing condition.
rows.anchor: وأخبر عن أصحاب الكهف بالعجب وإنما العجب حالهم في قومهم ، فثم مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kahf is a broad, central cleft in a mountain; a narrower opening is called a cave.
rows.anchor: والكهف : الشق المتسع الوسط في جبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raqim is a written tablet carried by the sleepers; reported explanations say it recorded their monotheism, their religious book, or the reason they fled persecution.
rows.anchor: والرقيم : فعيل بمعنى مفعول من الرقم وهو الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran begins the story with its reliable lesson and exemplary model: the youths taking refuge in their Lord and receiving His response.
rows.anchor: وابتدأ القرآن من قصتهم بمحل العبرة الصادقة والقدوة الصالحة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story concerns righteous people who fled widespread paganism, slept for a long time, and awoke after their persecutors had passed; God may then have kept them alive or preserved their bodies after death.
rows.anchor: وقد أشارت الآية إلى قصة نفر من صالحي الأمم السالفة ثبتوا على دين الحق

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most accounts place the cave at Absus, near Tarsus between Aleppo and Armenia, not Ephesus in Greece; Ibn Ashur says commentators confused the similar names.
rows.anchor: والذي ذكره الأكثر أن في بلد يقال له ( أبسس ) بفتح الهمزة وسكون الموحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the account summarized from Ibn Atiyya, the youths lived under Emperor Decius, who persecuted Christians; they fled to Mount Benjelus and were put to sleep when the king pursued them.
rows.anchor: وكانوا في زمن الأنبراطور ( دوقيوس ) ويقال ( دقيانوس ) الذي ملك

rows.speaker: ابن العبري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ibri estimates their sleep at 240 years, while the Quran gives 300 years.
rows.anchor: وقد بقوا في رقدتهم مدة طويلة قربها ابن العبري بمائتين وأربعين سنة ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After awakening, one youth returned to Absus with old coins to buy food; the changed city and currency astonished him and its people, and the youths' death after visitors arrived served as a sign affirming Christianity.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الله جعلهم آية لأنفسهم وللناس فبعثهم من مرقدهم ولم يعلموا مدة مكثهم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari's account names Arius and Atius, city leaders, among those who visited; another report says the governor wrote to the Roman emperor, who visited and ordered a mosque built, though its completion is unknown.
rows.anchor: والذي في ( كتاب الطبري ) أن الذين ذهبوا إلى مشاهدة أصحاب الكهف هم رئيسا المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave may later have collapsed in an earthquake, while many false identifications arose; sites in Tunisia are called the Seven Sleepers because people assume the youths numbered seven.
rows.anchor: ولعله قد انهدم بحادث زلزال أو نحوه كرامة من الله لأصحابه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report cited through Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim, Muawiya sought to see the sleepers; Ibn Abbas objected by citing the warning that a viewer would flee, and God drove the men away with wind.
rows.anchor: وفي ( تفسير الألوسي ) عن ابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: A report through Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim says Ibn Abbas, campaigning with Habib ibn Maslama, found bones at the cave and said the sleepers' bones had vanished more than 300 years earlier.
rows.anchor: وروى عبد الرزاق وابن أبي حاتم عن عكرمة : أن ابن عباس غزا مع حبيب

rows.speaker: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي
rows.claim: A report from al-Qaffal says al-Wathiq sent al-Khwarizmi to inspect the cave; he saw bodies with hair on their chests and judged their preservation artificial, using drugs such as aloe.
rows.anchor: عن القفال عن محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي المنجم : ( أن الواثق أنفذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Wathiq expedition rests on the mistaken identification with Ephesus; Ephesus remained Byzantine, while Absus belonged to Muslim lands.
rows.anchor: مبني على اعتقادهم أن الكهف كان حول مدينة ( أفسوس ) بالفاء أخت القاف وهو وهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says he visited a cave near Loja by Granada in 1104, containing bodies and a dog's remains, with a nearby Roman building called al-Raqim; he could find no prior account identifying them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : ( وبالأندلس في جهة ( أغرناطة ) بقرب قرية تسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sleepers' story is tied to a major historical phase in the spread of true religions, especially Christianity.
rows.anchor: وقصة أهل الكهف لها اتصال بتاريخ طور كبير من أطوار ظهور الأديان الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persecuted Christians often sheltered and worshipped in caves, buried their dead there, and took dogs for protection, so Ibn Atiyya's cave could be one such burial place.
rows.anchor: وقد كان المتنصرون يضطهدون في البلاد فكانوا يفرون من المدن والقرى إلى الكهوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Jews reportedly prompted the question, the sleepers may instead have been Jewish: Jews shunned Christian accounts, and caves near Tunis were identified by a Christian archaeologist as Jewish refuges from Roman Carthaginian persecution.
rows.anchor: غير أن ما ذكر في سبب نزول السورة من علم اليهود بأهل الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Jews and Christians may each have known a story about their own righteous people, or both may have claimed one group, explaining differing locations.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون لأهل كلتا الملتين اليهودية والنصرانية خبرا عن قوم من صالحيهم

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says the sleepers belonged to a non-Arab nation and Christians knew and dated their story.
rows.anchor: قال السهيلي في ( الروض الأنف ) : وأصحاب الكهف من أمة عجمية

none: The segment contains only the verse heading and text, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public speculation about the youths' number and sleep's duration continued after revelation; the Quran leaves the matter vague to train believers to avoid inquiries with no religious or human benefit.
rows.anchor: فكانت مثار تخرصات في معرفة عددهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unintroduced they means people or Muslims; discussing the count is not itself sinful, but no claim has proof, and the future tense predicts continued debate.
rows.anchor: وضمير ( يقولون ) عائد إلى غير مذكور لأنه معلوم من المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning seven and eight does not hint that eight was the true number; the Quran explicitly calls unsupported guesses speculation.
rows.anchor: وليس في الانتهاء إلى عدد الثمانية إيماء إلى أنه العدة في نفس الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A few people know the count because God informed them; Muhammad must be among them, and Ibn Abbas reportedly said he was one of the few.
rows.anchor: وقد أعلم الله أن قليلا من الخلق يعلمون عدتهم وهم من أطلعهم الله على ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly identified himself as one of the few who know their number.
rows.anchor: وروي أن ابن عباس قال : أنا من القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may have favored an odd number as auspicious, but there is no evidence for this, and God calls their assertion a guess at the unseen.
rows.anchor: وكأن أقوال الناس تمالأت على أن عدتهم فردية تيمنا بعدد المفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajm literally means throwing stones and is metaphorically used for speaking without reflection or verification; Zuhayr's poetry witnesses the figurative sense.
rows.anchor: والرجم حقيقته : الرمي بحجر ونحوه . واستعير هنا لرمي الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two clauses about the dog may each be an adjective of the preceding number or a second predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: وكل من جملة { رابعهم كلبهم } وجملة { سادسهم كلبهم } في موضع الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw before the eighth count marks a circumstantial clause, not an emphatic adjective; al-Sakkaki and other scholars reject al-Kashshaf's analysis as unidiomatic.
rows.anchor: ولا وجه لجعل الواو فيه داخلة على جملة هي صفة للنكرة لقصد تأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to say that God knows best answers the audience's desire for a reliable count: God's knowledge is complete, while others' knowledge is conjectural.
rows.anchor: فأجيب بأن يحال العلم بذلك على علام الغيوب . وإسناد اسم التفضيل إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that only a few know answers whether any human has partial knowledge; they must have been informed by God and remain less knowing than Him.
rows.anchor: فأجيب بأن قليلا من الناس يعلمون ذلك ولا محالة هم من أطلعهم الله على ذلك بوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Meccan opponents dispute the number based on scriptural reports, the Prophet should not debate them because the issue has no useful consequence.
rows.anchor: فلا تمارهم إذ هو اشتغال بما ليس فيه جدوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mirāʾ derives from doubt and, through reciprocal verbal form, describes disputation that draws both sides into doubt; it became conventional for argument.
rows.anchor: والتماري : تفاعل مشتق من المرية ، وهي الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permitted outward argument is brief and undeniable, such as saying God knows their number and only a few know it; further inquiry lacks evidence and benefit.
rows.anchor: والمراء الظاهر : هو الذي لا سبيل إلى إنكاره ولا يطول الخوض فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istifta means seeking authoritative information about something not commonly known, and fi-him means concerning the sleepers' affair.
rows.anchor: والاستفتاء : طلب الفتوى ، وهي الخبر عن أمر علمي مما لا يعلمه كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the prohibition as implying that the Meccans who asked did not themselves know the story's details.
rows.anchor: والمراد من النهي عن استفتائهم الكناية عن جهلهم بأمر أهل الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the prohibition can imply that the Prophet already knows the truth from God and need not ask, while he is not commanded to satisfy the challengers; Ibn Ashur says this explains the prohibition's purpose.
rows.anchor: أو يكون كناية رمزية عن حصول علم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بحقيقة أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase from among them cannot refer to the People of the Book, since transmitters and commentators agree that the surah is Meccan.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه الآيات مكية باتفاق الرواة والمفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of gardens elaborates the previously summarized reward; the demonstrative highlights that believers who had faith and righteous deeds deserve it.
rows.anchor: الجملة مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا ، لأن ما أجمل من عدم إضاعة أجرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive lām denotes ownership, and min marks the source of the rivers; the wording recalls the promise in al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: واللام في { لهم جنات عدن } لام الملك . و ( من ) للابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying rivers flow beneath them instead of beneath the gardens reinforces their possession through several overlapping emphases, also intended to enrage the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: ووجه إيثار إضافة ( تحت ) إلى ضميرهم دون ضمير الجنات زيادة تقرير المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuhallawna is passive because the believers find themselves adorned by God's creation; asawir is an irregular plural, and its plural-of-plural form may suggest varied jeweled designs.
rows.anchor: وأسند الفعل إلى المجهول ، لأنهم يجدون أنفسهم محلين بتكوين الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhfash treats min before bracelets as an emphatic addition; those who reject addition in affirmative clauses take it as indicating origin, a reading Ibn Ashur says is necessary for them.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله : { من أساور } مزيدة للتأكيد على رأي الأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A siwar is a gold or silver armlet; investigators identify the word as borrowed from Persian.
rows.anchor: والسوار : حلي من ذهب أو فضة يحيط بموضع من الذراع ، وهو اسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min before gold is explanatory; silver is omitted here because the Human surah mentions it elsewhere, and each metal has its own beauty.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله : { من ذهب } فإن ( من ) فيه للبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clothing covers the body with a garment for protection and adornment; thawb means a woven length of cloth, and green was considered balanced for sight and a royal color.
rows.anchor: واللباس : ستر البدن بثوب من قميص أو إزار أو رداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is fine brocade worn directly against skin beneath the coarser istabraq, which is thick brocade woven with gold thread and worn over it.
rows.anchor: والسندس : صنف من الثياب ، وهو الديباج الرقيق يلبس مباشرا للجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is borrowed; some call its source Persian, while investigators trace it to Indian sandun, passed through Roman sindus into Arabic.
rows.anchor: فأما لفظ ( سندس ) فلا خلاف في أنه معرب وإنما اختلفوا في أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Authorities disagree on istabraq's source: Ibn Durayd says Syriac, Ibn Qutayba says Roman, while others derive it from Persian forms; it takes a hamzat al-qat and plural abariq.
rows.anchor: وأما الإستبرق فهو معرب عن الفارسية . وأصله في الفارسية

rows.speaker: ابن النقيب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Naqib argues that no eloquent substitute could match istabraq: the term uniquely names heavy silk, the highest worldly garment, suited to a promise of rewards desired by all.
rows.anchor: وفي الإتقان } للسيوطي عن ابن النقيب : لو اجتمع فصحاء العالم وأرادوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min before sundus is explanatory; ornaments precede clothing because they embellish the gardens, while clothing is closer to the inhabitants, the reverse order from the Human surah.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله : { من سندس } للبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutta'akiin describes relaxed reclining; ara'ik are beds combined with canopies, a mark of luxury, and reclining is also mentioned in Joseph's story.
rows.anchor: وجملة متكئين فيها على الأرائك } في موضع الحال من ضمير { يلبسون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise formula has an omitted object understood as the gardens; hasunat functions like a formula of praise and contrasts with the description of Hell's resting place.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : نعم الثواب الجنات الموصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur speculates the gardens may have been near Taif, where Meccans had orchards.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر المفسرون أين كانت الجنتان ، ولعلهما كانتا بالطائف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two men were Israelite brothers who inherited money: one bought land and built gardens, while the other gave his wealth away.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : هما أخوان من بني إسرائيل مات أبوهما وترك لهما مالا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Some commentators cited by Ibn Atiyya treat the pair as an imagined case; this would be a vivid comparison of one conceivable state with another, like the garden parable in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وإن كان حال الرجلين حالا مفروضا كما جوزه بعض المفسرين فيما نقله عنه ابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative is more likely historical: its unprefixed dialogue and the later report of the man's defeat resemble remembered events and make the warning more forceful.
rows.anchor: والأظهر من سياق الكلام وصنع التراكيب مثل قوله : قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ja'alna means that God determined the means for the gardens; the vocabulary recalls the garden of palms and grapes in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: ومعنى جعلنا لأحدهما } قدرنا له أسباب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafafna means surrounded; gardens are enhanced when encircled by fruit trees, as the same root describes angels around the Throne.
rows.anchor: ومعنى حففناهما } أحطناهما ، يقال : حفه بكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamar with two dammas means abundant, varied wealth, including money, livestock, gardens, and fields; it figuratively derives from the fruiting of one's assets.
rows.anchor: والثمر بضم الثاء والميم : المال الكثير المختلف من النقدين والأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabigha's verse attests the metaphor of wealth bearing fruit, and his other line uses athmara for wealth and children.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة : فلما رأى أن ثمر الله ماله وأثل موجودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read thamar with two dammas; Abu Amr and Yaqub use a sukun on the second consonant, while Asim reads both vowels as fatha, with the latter taken as a plural indicating many kinds of earnings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ثمر } بضم المثلثة وضم الميم . وقرأه أبو عمرو ويعقوب

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaalab recounts that al-Hajjaj threatened to cut the tongue of anyone reading thamar with two dammas; al-A'mash's response was not to follow that threat and he used that reading.
rows.anchor: وعن النحاس بسنده إلى ثعلب عن الأعمش : أن الحجاح قال : لو سمعت أحدا يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner had additional wealth besides the two gardens; the preceding abundance naturally led him to boast, and sahib here means the other man paired with him in the parable.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : وكان لصاحب الجنتين مال ، أي غير الجنتين . والفاء لتفريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dialogue shows the poorer man had admonished his companion about faith and righteous conduct; the rich man answered with arrogance rather than fair argument.
rows.anchor: ودل فعل المحاورة على أن صاحبه قد وعظه في الإيمان والعمل الصالح ، فراجعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A'azz means greater in strength and honor, linked to numerous kin and courage; nafar means the man's fighting kin and here his sons, as verse 40 confirms, and it is a specification of the comparison.
rows.anchor: والنفر : عشيرة الرجل الذين ينفرون معه . وأراد بهم هنا ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He entered one garden first, which explains the singular although he owned two; he was unjust to himself by associating partners with God and denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { وهو ظالم لنفسه } وهو مشرك مكذب بالبعث بطر بنعمة الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabid means perish; abad here means a very long duration, not endless survival, and the owner's confidence came from the trees' strength and abundant water and shade.
rows.anchor: والأبد : مراد منه طول المدة ، أي هي باقية بقاء أمثالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man's denial of the Hour does not logically follow from confidence in his garden; he uses it to taunt the believer and mocks the believer's expectation of divine reward.
rows.anchor: ولا تلازم بين المعتقدين . ولكنه أراد التورك على صاحبه المؤمن تخطئة إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional boast that he would find a better return is sarcastic, as in al-As ibn Wa'il's reported taunt to Khabbab ibn al-Aratt about being repaid in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقول العاصي بن وائل السهمي لخباب بن الأرت ( ليكونن لي مال هنالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of oath and emphatic nūn intensify the sarcasm; munqalaban is a specification meaning the place to which one returns.
rows.anchor: وأكد كلامه بلام القسم ونون التوكيد مبالغة في التهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use the dual pronoun referring back to both gardens, while Abu Amr, Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, Yaqub, and Khalaf read the singular to match the later singular references.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب وخلف منها } بالإفراد

none: The segment contains only the verse text and heading, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense account of his saying conveys repeated regret after punishment, when regret can no longer help.
rows.anchor: وجملة ويقول } حكاية لتندمه على ما فرط منه حين لا ينفعه الندم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative signals anguish; laytani personifies the wish as something called to appear, and the lament implies that he now believes in God alone.
rows.anchor: وهذا ندم على الإشراك فيما مضى وهو يؤذن بأنه آمن بالله وحده حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that no faction helped him rebukes his earlier boast about having a greater following; his former group could not protect him from punishment.
rows.anchor: وقوله : ولم تكن له فئة ينصرونه من دون الله } موعظة وتنبيه على جزاء قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi'a means a group, and the following clause describes the kind of group he lacked: one capable of helping him against God's punishment.
rows.anchor: والفئة : الجماعة . وجملة { ينصرونه } صفة ، أي لم تكن له فئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause means he had no ability to escape or free himself from punishment.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وما كان منتصرا } أي ولا يكون له انتصار وتخلص من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use feminine takun to match fi'a; Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf use masculine yakun, both allowed when the subject is not grammatically feminine in a strict sense.
rows.anchor: وقرأه الجمهور { ولم تكن } بمثناة فوقية اعتدادا بتأنيث { فئة } في اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His downfall was not simply for disbelief, since disbelievers may be allowed long lives; it punished his arrogance in using wealth to belittle a poor believer and reject God's promise.
rows.anchor: وأحاط به هذا العقاب لا لمجرد الكفر ، لأن الله قد يمتع كافرين كثيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like Qarun, he lost a blessing he had used to boast; the parable warns Meccan idolators who spurned poor believers and asked the Prophet to dismiss them.
rows.anchor: كما سلبت النعمة عن قارون حين قال : { إنما أوتيته على علم عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This conclusion summarizes and grounds the preceding claims: only God has protective authority, which could motivate help and rescue; the ruined man learned that his false gods gave him none.
rows.anchor: تذييل للجمل قبلها لما في هذه الجملة من العموم الحاصل من قصر الولاية على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distant demonstrative evokes an extraordinary state as though it were a distant place; in such a condition authority belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: واسم إشارة المكان البعيد مستعار للإشارة إلى الحال العجيبة بتشبيه الحالة بالمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read wilaya with kasra, as a verbal noun or a term for sovereignty, while the majority read walaya with fatha.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة والكسائي وخلف الولاية } بكسر الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read al-haqq in the genitive as a description of God; Abu Amr, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read it nominative as a description of true authority, since other claims of authority are false.
rows.anchor: و { الحق } قرأه الجمهور بالجر ، على أنه وصف لله تعالى

rows.speaker: حجة الإسلام
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali explains that God is intrinsically the Real and is called true in relation to the intellect that perceives Him as He is.
rows.anchor: قال حجة الإسلام : ( والواجب بذاته هو الحق مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic addressee of seeing the exposed earth is any observer; its surface stands bare without plants, trees, or animals, like the plain at resurrection.
rows.anchor: والبارزة : الظاهرة ، أي الظاهر سطحها ، إذ ليس عليها شيء يستر وجهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause We gathered them can be circumstantial under either active or passive readings of moving the mountains, or can coordinate with the future after using the past to stress certainty.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن نجعل جملة وحشرناهم } معطوفة على جملة { نسير الجبال }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maghadara means leaving something behind; the pronouns for gathering, the people, and their presentation refer back to those addressed in the worldly-life parable.
rows.anchor: والمغادرة : إبقاء شيء وتركه من تعلق فعل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Presentation means bringing people forward so their condition can be seen; the image borrows from a military review, as in a hadith about nations being presented.
rows.anchor: وعرض الشيء : إحضاره ليرى حاله وما يحتاجه . ومنه عرض الجيش على الأمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing in one unobstructed row exposes every guilty person and creates dread; the presentation clause also describes the immediate state of the gathered people.
rows.anchor: والصف : جماعة يقفون واحدا حذو واحد بحيث يبدو جميعهم لا يحجب أحد منهم أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God your Lord instead of saying Our Lord dignifies the addressee and makes the threatening presentation an act of support against those who denied his warning of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن الإضمار إلى التعريف بالإضافة في قوله : { على ربك } دون أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They came to Us is unintroduced direct speech understood from the address and functions circumstantially; the resurrected audience hears it from God as a threat and reproach for denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لقد جئتمونا } مقول لقول محذوف دل عليه أن الجملة خطاب للمعروضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming is a metaphor for being present: death had made them seem absent, and resurrection is like the absent returning.
rows.anchor: والمجيء : مجاز في الحضور ، شبهوا حين موتهم بالغائبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison to the first creation makes the second creation resemble the first and refutes denial of resurrection, as another verse argues.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { كما خلقناكم أول مرة } واقع موقع المفعول المطلق المفيد للمشابهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal shifts from threat and indirect rebuke to an explicit charge of error; the statement describes their false belief rather than merely asserting its content.
rows.anchor: والإضراب في قوله : بل زعمتم ألن نجعل لكم موعدا } انتقال من التهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Za'm is mistaken belief or a claim exposed to falsity; maw'id normally means a promised time or place and here means the promised time of resurrection.
rows.anchor: والزعم : الإعتقاد المخطىء ، أو الخبر المعرض للكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The books are placed as part of the gathered people's state; the singular generic book means each person's deeds record, as other verses describe.
rows.anchor: والكتاب مراد به الجنس ، أي وضعت كتب أعمال البشر ، لأن لكل أحد كتابا

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali suggests the singular may be one comprehensive book combining what is distributed among individual records.
rows.anchor: وعن الغزالي : أنه قال : يكون كتاب جامع لجميع ما هو متفرق في الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic seeing address is not specifically to the Prophet, who will be in an exalted station at that time; ishfaq means fear of something to come.
rows.anchor: والخطاب بقوله : { فترى } لغير معين . وليس للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense makes the terrifying scene vivid or conveys the frightened people's repeated lament; calling on woe is a conventional expression of pain.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالمضارع في { يقولون } لاستحضار الحالة الفظيعة ، أو لإفادة تكرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about what is wrong with the book expresses astonishment; ma is an interrogative meaning what, and this book specifies it.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام في قولهم : مال هذا الكتاب } مستعمل في التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in their question denotes association, as in asking why someone does not trust Joseph.
rows.anchor: واللام للاختصاص مثل قوله : { ما لك لا تأمنا على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the book leaves nothing out is a circumstantial clause that explains their astonishment; small and large mean deeds, whose scale can reflect visibility or strength.
rows.anchor: والصغيرة والكبيرة : وصفان لموصوف محذوف لدلالة المقام ، أي فعلة أو هنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Small deeds come first because recording even the least is especially astonishing; the exception means every deed is counted without omission, not that any case escapes counting.
rows.anchor: وتقديم ذكر الصغيرة لأنها أهم من حيث يتعلق التعجب من إحصائها . وعطفت عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record displays every deed immediately and in detail, so people find all they did present before them through an extraordinary process.
rows.anchor: والإحصاء : العد ، أي كانت أفعالهم معدودة مفصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's justice means the book contains only their own acts, not anything they never did; duties, warnings, and promises preceded judgment, so punishment is not injustice.
rows.anchor: أي لم يحمل عليهم شيء لم يعملوه ، لأن الله لا يظلم أحدا فيؤاخذه

none: The segment contains only the verse heading and text, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to recall Adam's creation continues the moral warning about following desire and despising virtue: it contrasts the world's beginning with the preceding account of its end.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { ويوم نسير الجيال ( الكهف : 47 ) بتقدير : واذكر إذ قلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story also prepares for the summons to call false partners in verse 52, since Satan's deception led people to associate others with God.
rows.anchor: وهذا أيضا تمهيد وتوطئة لقوله : ويوم يقول نادوا شركائي الذين زعمتم } الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story parallels earlier criticism of the wealthy who scorned poor Muslims; Satan is the root of misguidance, and ultimate loss follows his and his allies' steps.
rows.anchor: فكان في قصة إبليس نحو آدم مثل لهم ، ولأن في هذه القصة تذكيرا بأن الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran repeats this story with a lesson tailored to each setting: al-Baqara presents beginnings, while this surah uses it as a parallel and preparation for rebuke.
rows.anchor: وهذه القصة تكررت في مواضع كثيرة من القرآن ، وهي في كل موضع تشتمل على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasaqa means departing from obedience, metaphorically modeled on a date escaping its skin; Abu Ubayda, al-Mubarrad, and Ibn al-Arabi say this usage was unknown in pre-Islamic poetry and speech.
rows.anchor: وفسق : تجاوز عن طاعته . وأصله قولهم : فسقت الرطبة ، إذا خرجت من قشرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Iblis and his descendants did not witness creation, they cannot be partners in it or deserve worship; this argument addresses polytheists who already recognize God's sole creative power.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لما لم يشهدوا خلق السماوات والأرض لم يكونوا شركاء لله في الخلق بطريق الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing creation means being present in order to participate or assist; its denial rules out divinity a fortiori, since the heavens were made before Iblis existed.
rows.anchor: والإشهاد : جعل الغير شاهدا ، أي حاضرا ، وهو هنا كناية عن إحضار خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prior nonexistence disproves divinity: whatever can be nonexistent cannot be eternal, while eternity is required of God.
rows.anchor: فهو استدلال على انتفاء إلهيتهم بسبق العدم على وجودهم . وكل ما جاز عليه العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns for those not made witnesses and for themselves refer to Iblis and his descendants; themselves means some of one another, since no creature can witness its own creation.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { أنفسهم } ، أنفس بعضهم بقرينة استحالة مشاهدة المخلوق خلق نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth were created before their inhabitants; pre-Islamic Arabs nevertheless believed spirits controlled the land and sought a valley's spirit for protection.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الله تعالى خلق السماوات والأرض قبل أن يخلق لهما سكانهما كما دل عليه
